Present Continuous for Future Arrangements in Affirmative
We generally use the present continuous tense to talk about activities that are developing right now. However, it has another important use, you can also use it to express activities in the future.
The supervisor is visiting us next week and everything is a mess.
Are you doing anything this afternoon?

Depending on the context, you use the present continuous tense to express arrangements or plans. This use implies that more people, apart from the speaker, are conscious and know about the event. It is also implicit that there is certain preparation or planning for the activity to take place or happen.

 

The structure for the present continuous for arrangements is:

 

Subject + auxiliary verb to be + main verb (-ing form) + time complement

 

Examples:

  • I am starting a Java class next Monday.
  • We are launching the program tomorrow morning.

 

In the previous examples, you can see that the time complement suggests the action is taking place in the future. Always pay attention to the time complement in the sentence to avoid mistakes, as you can confuse it with the present continuous for actions happening right now.

However, it isn’t mandatory to use a time complement each time you need to talk about arrangements using the present continuous tense.
Verbs + Objects + Infinitives
Certain verbs can have a direct object followed by another verb in infinitive.
My boss told me to talk to talk to you.
I want you to give me some advice on how to manage and organize our databases.
I need you to listen to me very carefully.
Is there anything else you can advise us to do?

There are some verbs that can include a second person in the action, apart from the principal subject or performer of the activity. This secondary character in the sentence is the object of the verb. Some of these verbs include ask, help, invite, need, tell, advice, order, persuade, want, etc.
For example: Janet asked Luisa to check the program for bugs.

The Hash Function
The hash function creates a value also known as the hashing algorithm which is very useful when searching databases.

A hash function normally groups a number of characters, known as a key, and relates them to a value of a determined length, called a hash value or hash. This hash value represents the original string of characters or key, however, it is usually shorter than the original. The hash function is also referred to as hashing.

Hashing is used for tracing elements and creating indexes in databases since it is simpler to find the abbreviated version of the item or hash value, than the longer original value. In other words, hashing is used with a database to have items retrieved more quickly, by using a shorter version of such item.
In addition, you can also use the hashing function; it is helpful to have items retrieved faster, by using a shorter version of such item.

images.text:
Jaime: Hi George! My boss told me to talk to you. He said you can help us solve a problem we have in our department. Are you doing anything this afternoon?
George: Actually, I am going to the dentist after lunch. I have an appointment, but we can talk right now. Is it OK?
Jaime: Yeah, no problem. I want you to give me some advice on how to manage and organize our databases. The supervisor is visiting us next week and everything is a mess.
George: OK. I need you to listen to me very carefully. In my opinion, what your department needs is a data dictionary; it is basically a modern database that keeps track of the elements of another database.

Jaime: That sounds very interesting. What else can you tell me about it?
George: Well, a data dictionary creates a collection of descriptions of separate data in a database. To start with, you have to identify each element and its relationship to other elements; experts call this process "data modeling". It produces a representation of object relationships where all elements receive a name, then the system defines their relationships in a brief text. Finally, it organizes this collection of definitions for reference into a book, this book is the data dictionary.

Jaime: A data dictionary seems like the solution we need. Is there anything else you can advise us to do?
George: If you develop software that uses a database, a data dictionary is one of the best ways to make quick views, as well as to understand where a data item fits in the structure and what values it can have. In addition, you can also use the hashing function; it is helpful to have items retrieved faster, by using a shorter version of such item.
Jaime: Thanks, George! You're very kind.
